subject: EVG Labs — post-demo tech recap & routing / policy next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@evglabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: EVG Labs — post-demo tech recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from the product/infra side so we have alignment for the integration sprint:

1) Goals from EVG: embed LLM answers in search results + reranker over candidate titles; keep 95th pct latency < 200ms for UI queries; target unit cost ~$0.015–0.025 per active request.
2) Recommended approach: local routing for low-latency UIs -> small L1 model (quantized) with prefix caching; fallback chain to larger L2 model for long-tail queries.
3) SDK & auth: start with Redwood JS SDK v1.4.2 (we'll provide a private npm link). Auth options: API key scoped to project for PoC; for production we recommend mTLS or short-lived tokens (OIDC).
4) Structured output/tool-calling: we propose a 3-field JSON schema (answer, sources[], action_hint) and to enable tool-calling through the SDK’s tool interface for entity lookups.
5) Embeddings/rerank: produce embeddings with the 1536-d model; store vectors in your existing Pinecone index (we can provide compatibility shim) and run an initial reranker pass in Redwood to reduce API load.

Action items (proposed):
- EVG: send sample dataset (10–20 queries + expected outputs) and SOC2 contact details (Tim).
- Redwood: share SDK install + quickstart repo, sample routing policy (latency threshold + cost caps), and a draft SOW.

Attachments: evg-demo-reqs.pdf (meeting notes), evg-sample-schema.csv (sample user queries).

Can you confirm access for a short technical kickoff next Wednesday 4/28?

— Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Latency SLO: 95th pct <200ms is our target, but for external search we can tolerate up to 350ms for complex queries.
- Dataset: attaching an export of 12 production search queries (sanitized).
- Security: looped in Tim (SOC2 lead) — he’ll ask for an evidence list.

I can do 4/28 for the kickoff. Please include a short runbook for failure modes (e.g., model OOM -> fallback to cached vector response).

— Maya

Adding a few technical notes and a sample routing policy snippet we recommend for the PoC. Paste into your policy YAML in the console or SDK call: 

# sample routing policy (PoC)
priority: ["low_latency_pool", "balanced_pool", "cost_pool"]
rules:
  - name: ui_low_latency
    match: request.path == '/api/search' && request.latency_budget_ms <= 200
    route_to: low_latency_pool
    max_tokens: 256
    model_fallback: ["l1-quant", "l2-8bit"]
  - name: background_rerank
    match: request.path == '/api/rerank'
    route_to: cost_pool
    max_tokens: 512
    model_fallback: ["l2-8bit"]

Auth note: for PoC we'll create project-scoped API keys with tightened quota. For the production rollout we can enable short-lived OIDC tokens with our token broker (supports Okta/GCP/AD).

I'll upload the quickstart repo and a sandbox policy to the Drive link Neha will share.

— Aditya
Principal Engineer, Platform

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple security asks before we share more PII-like samples: 
1) SOC2 report (latest) and a list of in-scope controls for the inference path.
2) Data retention policy for request logs and KV cache — we need default retention <=90 days and option to shorten to 30.
3) Clarify key management: do you support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS)?

If Redwood can provide those items we’ll move forward with the sample dataset and procurement.

— Tim Roberts
Head of Security, EVG Labs

Thanks Tim — quick responses below and next actions so we don't lose momentum.

Security answers:
- SOC2: attaching our latest SOC2 type II summary (will send full report under NDA).
- Retention: default request logs 90 days; we support 30/7/0 retention profiles at project level. KV cache TTLs can be set per-model/prefix; we'll provide a config template.
- KMS: yes, we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For on-prem/private deployments we also offer HSM integrations.

Next actions & timeline:
- Redwood (Aditya/Karthik): upload SDK quickstart, sandbox routing policy, and sample runbook to Drive by EOD 4/23.
- EVG (Maya/Tim): confirm NDA path for SOC2 and upload sanitized dataset by 4/26.
- Mutual: 4/28 technical kickoff (30–45m) — propose 9:00am PT.

Procurement: I’ll circulate a draft SOW (redwood-sow-draft.docx) via DocuSign after we confirm timelines; estimate for the PoC (4 weeks) will be in the SOW.

Links: HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/evg-labs; Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4dEvG-demo; DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-evg-2027
